title: Yenisei Kyrgyz
capsule: The Yenisei Kyrgyz were a Turkic-speaking people of the upper Yenisei River basin whose political history spans from at least the 6th century AD through the Mongol era. Their most dramatic moment came in 840 AD when they destroyed the Uyghur Khaganate — sacking its capital Ordu-Baliq on the Orkhon — and briefly held sway over much of the Mongolian steppe in an episode sometimes called the Kyrgyz Great Migration. The Yenisei Kyrgyz lacked the administrative capacity to hold that empire and by the late 9th century had retreated to their Minusinsk homeland; they submitted peacefully to Genghis Khan in the early 13th century and their distinct polity dissolved into the Mongol imperial structure, though related populations persisted as the Khakass of the Yenisei basin.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Yenisei Kyrgyz homeland in the Minusinsk Basin is well attested archaeologically (Tashtyk and Yenisei runic inscriptions), but the extent of their 9th-century steppe empire is poorly defined; the outer limits are reconstructed from Chinese Tang sources and are inherently approximate.
